title: Tea and toast

clues.t: 67-year-old man, living alone since his wife died.
Gums bleed when he brushes his teeth.
Painful legs and swollen ankles.
Tiny bleeds around hair follicles on his shins, with corkscrew-shaped hairs.
A leg graze from 2 months ago still hasn't healed.
Diet is mostly toast and tea. No fruit or vegetables.

pearl: Not just a sailor's disease. It still turns up with restrictive diets, alcohol use disorder and in older men living alone. Symptoms respond within days of vitamin C replacement.

title: Pins, needles, pills

clues.t: 62-year-old man with tingling in both feet for 6 months.
Unsteady walking in the dark. Fine with the lights on.
Type 2 diabetes for 12 years, HbA1c well controlled.
Sore, smooth, red tongue.
Hb 128 g/L · MCV 106 fL
On metformin 1 g twice daily since diagnosis.

pearl: Not every neuropathy in diabetes is diabetic. Long-term metformin lowers B12 absorption, and neurological damage can occur before anaemia appears. Check B12 (or holotranscobalamin) periodically.

title: Salt of the earth

clues.t: 34-year-old woman. Exhausted, lost 6 kg without trying.
Craves salty food. Adds salt to her chips twice.
Light-headed on standing. Nauseated most mornings.
Palmar creases and gums look darker than her baseline.
Na 128 mmol/L · K 5.7 mmol/L
9 am cortisol 62 nmol/L · ACTH markedly raised

pearl: Hyponatraemia with hyperkalaemia is the tell. Raised ACTH means the problem is in the adrenal (primary), which causes the pigmentation. If she's unwell, give hydrocortisone before you wait on tests.

title: Slaughterhouse fever

clues.t: 38-year-old man with high fevers and sweats for 5 days.
Severe headache behind the eyes and aching muscles.
Dry cough. Chest X-ray shows patchy changes.
ALT 140 U/L · Platelets 98 ×10⁹/L
Lives in the Upper Hunter. Not vaccinated against anything since school.
Works at an abattoir processing cattle and goats.

pearl: Ask every febrile patient what they do for work. Q fever is notifiable. Prevention is Q-Vax, but workers need skin and serology testing first because vaccinating someone already immune can cause severe reactions.

title: After the dentist

clues.t: 63-year-old man with fevers and night sweats for 3 weeks.
Lost 4 kg. Aching joints. "Feels like a flu that won't leave."
He had a tooth extracted 6 weeks ago.
He has a known heart murmur from rheumatic fever as a child.
Thin dark streaks under two fingernails. Tender red lumps on his finger pads.
2 of 3 blood cultures grow viridans streptococci

pearl: Take three sets of blood cultures before any antibiotics. Splinter haemorrhages and Osler's nodes are late but classic. Prolonged fever plus a murmur is endocarditis until proven otherwise.

title: Dark on the windowsill

clues.t: 26-year-old woman with severe abdominal pain. Third ED visit this year.
CT, ultrasound and scopes have all been normal.
Anxious and confused this time. Her arms feel weak.
Na 124 mmol/L
Attacks follow crash diets. This one started after a new medicine.
A urine sample left on the windowsill turned dark reddish-brown

pearl: Severe abdominal pain with normal imaging, plus hyponatraemia or neurological signs, should prompt a urine porphobilinogen test during the attack. Fasting and many medicines can trigger attacks.

title: Slow burn

clues.t: 55-year-old man who has lost 12 kg over a year.
Chronic diarrhoea and bloating. Coeliac serology negative.
Years of migrating joint pains, long before any gut symptoms.
His skin has darkened and he runs low-grade fevers.
Now forgetful, with rhythmic jaw movements in time with slow eye convergence.
Duodenal biopsy: PAS-positive foamy macrophages

pearl: Caused by Tropheryma whipplei. Joint pains often come years before the gut symptoms. Rhythmic eye convergence with jaw movement (oculomasticatory myorhythmia) is pathognomonic. Very treatable with antibiotics, fatal if missed.

title: Barely a sting

clues.t: 29-year-old tourist with severe lower back pain that came on suddenly.
Drenched in sweat. Vomiting. Says she feels like she's going to die.
She was swimming off a beach near Cairns in December, 40 minutes ago.
She felt a small prick on her arm. Barely a mark there now.
Troponin rising

pearl: The sting is often trivial, then severe pain, sweating, hypertension and dread arrive 20–40 minutes later. Douse tropical stings with vinegar and call 000. It can cause heart failure, so monitor in hospital.

title: Hot is cold

clues.t: 45-year-old man with vomiting and diarrhoea, starting 4 hours after dinner.
Next day: tingling lips and fingers. His teeth ache, as if they're loose.
Cold drinks feel like they're burning his mouth.
HR 48
Three friends at the same dinner feel the same.
They ate a large Spanish mackerel caught on a trip off Queensland.

pearl: Hot–cold reversal is the giveaway. The toxin comes from large reef fish and isn't destroyed by cooking or freezing. Symptoms can last weeks. Advise avoiding alcohol and fish for a while, as both can bring symptoms back.

title: The night shift

clues.t: 49-year-old truck driver, exhausted despite 8 hours in bed.
Wakes with headaches most mornings.
Nodded off at the lights twice last week.
His partner moved to the spare room because of the snoring.
She says he stops breathing, then gasps.
BMI 34, collar size 46 cm, BP high on three medicines

pearl: Witnessed apnoeas plus daytime sleepiness is the classic pair. Untreated OSA drives resistant hypertension. Commercial drivers have specific fitness-to-drive standards in Australia.

title: Broken heart

clues.t: 66-year-old woman with sudden crushing chest pain.
It started at her husband's funeral this morning.
ECG: ST elevation in the anterior leads
Troponin raised
Coronary angiogram: no significant blockages
Echo: apex of the left ventricle balloons out, base contracts normally

pearl: It mimics a STEMI and must be managed as one until angiography. Usually triggered by emotional or physical stress in postmenopausal women. Function mostly recovers within weeks, but it isn't benign: complications and recurrence occur.

title: The renovator

clues.t: 38-year-old man with crampy abdominal pain and constipation for 2 months.
Irritable and forgetful. His partner says he's "not himself".
Hb 104 g/L, microcytic, but ferritin is normal
Blood film: basophilic stippling of red cells
He's been restoring a 1920s Newcastle terrace on weekends.
He dry-sands the old paint with no mask.

pearl: Australian homes built before 1970 often contain lead paint. NHMRC advises investigating a blood lead level above 5 µg/dL. Ask about hobbies and renovations, and check the whole household, especially children.

title: Sprint, then stop
answer: McArdle disease (glycogen storage disease type V)

clues.t: 22-year-old woman who has never once managed to run for a bus.
Since childhood, the first minutes of exercise bring cramps and stiffness.
If she slows down for a few minutes, she can then keep going for much longer.
After her first high-intensity gym class, her urine is the colour of cola.
CK 14,000 U/L, and it stays raised between episodes
Forearm exercise test: ammonia rises, lactate stays flat

pearl: Her muscles can't unlock their stored glycogen, so sprints starve them. The 'second wind' arrives when fats and glucose from the blood catch up. Described by Brian McArdle in London in 1951.

title: Moving target

clues.t: 48-year-old woman with vague, on-and-off tummy pain and bloating.
She resettled eight months ago, after ten years in a camp on the Thailand-Myanmar border.
An itchy rash around her waist and buttocks comes and goes.
It seems to creep several centimetres in an hour.
Eosinophils 1.9 ×10⁹/L
Serology positive for a soil-transmitted roundworm that can reinfect its own host.

pearl: The worm can reinfect the same person for decades, long after they've left an endemic area. Steroids can trigger a fatal overwhelming infection, which is why post-arrival screening for refugees and migrants matters. The fast-moving rash is larva currens, 'running larva'.

title: God bless us, every one

clues.t: 8-year-old girl, small for her age and often tired.
Her legs have started to bow. She broke a forearm in a minor fall.
Weak spells, with aching muscles.
Na 139 · K 2.8 · Cl 114 · HCO₃ 11 mmol/L · anion gap normal
Urine pH 6.8, despite her blood being acidic
Ultrasound: calcium deposits through the medullae on both sides

pearl: In 1992 a paediatric neurologist, Donald Lewis, argued in a journal that this could be what ailed Tiny Tim in Dickens' A Christmas Carol: short stature and weakness fit, it was deadly untreated, and Victorian alkaline remedies could have turned it around once Scrooge paid up.

title: 'Tis the season

clues.t: 5-year-old boy whose knee ballooned after a small tumble off his new bike.
He has always bruised easily, and bled for days after losing a tooth.
His mother's brother had the same trouble. His sister doesn't.
Platelets normal · PT normal · APTT prolonged
Factor VIII activity: normal
Factor IX activity: 3%

pearl: Named after Stephen Christmas, the five-year-old in whom it was first told apart from classic haemophilia. Rosemary Biggs and colleagues published it in the 1952 Christmas issue of the BMJ, and she defended the name as 'pleasantly provocative'. Stephen Christmas later became a haemophilia advocate.

title: Prawns and regret

clues.t: 58-year-old man woke at 3 am with a screaming pain in his foot.
The base of his big toe is red, hot and swollen. Even the bedsheet hurts.
Boxing Day. He had prawns, ham and "a few" beers yesterday.
He started a fluid tablet for his blood pressure last month.
Serum urate 0.38 mmol/L (upper normal)
Joint aspirate: needle-shaped crystals, negatively birefringent

pearl: Urate can be normal during a flare, so a normal level doesn't rule gout out. Thiazide diuretics raise urate. Joint aspiration showing crystals is the gold standard. Gout is especially common in Māori and Pacific men, largely because of inherited differences in how the body clears urate. It's not just the prawns.

title: One-sided story

clues.t: 71-year-old woman with burning pain around the right side of her chest for 3 days.
ECG and troponin are normal.
The pain stops exactly at the midline, front and back.
Her skin there is exquisitely tender to light touch.
Today, clusters of small blisters on a red base have appeared in a band.
She had chickenpox as a child.

pearl: Pain often comes 2–3 days before the rash. Start antivirals within 72 hours of rash onset. A blister on the tip of the nose (Hutchinson's sign) means the eye may be involved: refer urgently.

title: Ring doesn't fit

clues.t: 48-year-old man, sweating more than ever.
Partner says his snoring is now unbearable.
Had his wedding ring resized twice. Shoe size went up one.
Gaps have appeared between his lower teeth.
Carpal tunnel symptoms in both hands, new hypertension.
IGF-1 three times the upper limit of normal

pearl: Changes are so slow that family often miss them, so compare old photos. IGF-1 is the screening test; confirm with GH failing to suppress on a glucose tolerance test, then pituitary MRI.

title: Still open

clues.t: Baby girl born at 27 weeks, now 5 days old in the NICU.
She'd been improving, but now needs more breathing support again.
Her pulses feel unusually bounding, even in her palms.
A new murmur at the upper left sternal edge.
Echo: blood shunting left to right, from the aorta into the pulmonary artery

pearl: The ductus arteriosus usually closes within days of birth. In very premature babies it often stays open, so extra blood floods the lungs and runs off from the body: bounding pulses and a wide pulse pressure are the clues. Many close on their own; the NICU team decides whether it needs help. Happy World Prematurity Day to every early arrival and their families.

title: Cream crackers

clues.t: 52-year-old woman whose eyes feel gritty, like sand under the lids.
She can't eat a dry cracker without a glass of water.
Her dentist found five new cavities this year.
Both cheeks near her jaw are swollen and puffy.
Aching joints. Tired all the time.
Anti-Ro and anti-La antibodies positive

pearl: Dry eyes plus dry mouth is the core of it. Schirmer's test measures tear production. Lymphoma risk is raised, so a persistently enlarged parotid gland needs review.
